Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

Safari Ltd. Safariology The Solar System Arrived in a timely manner, only three days. A bit smaller than I expected even though there isn’t anything in the description concerning size. I like good close-ups but sometimes they give a false impression of size. But that’s going to work out for the 3-year old recipient that’s continually asking questions about outer space and the planets. Good quality and painted nicely, with maybe Mercury being an exception. Mercury is painted greyish and I always assumed its proximity to the sun would make it red, but what do I know?

It was received with an outburst of enthusiasm and made this grandpa very happy to witness this. I was also pleased to see that he quickly noticed that there were eight planets, instead of the nine that he expected. He had picked up on that somewhere, either through a book or perhaps a TV show. Scary smart this one is, then we had to explain why there is no Pluto. That’s not as easy as it may sound.

And to my profound relief it stated that this product is phthalate-free. No, I have no idea what that is either. Sounds pretty important though. I sure hope no phthalate was injured in the production.

We plan to make a mobile from this. I think that is pretty cool because it will always be within sight and not crammed into a toy box to be seen only once in a while. It’s also something I wish I had when I was a kid.

The float is hard to fully inflate, but even if it’s a little underinflated, it works great in the pool.

The bottom part is like an innertube and it’s comfortable for an adult to float in. There are small plastic handles on each side of the innertube, which reminds me of a raft at a water park. The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. This allows for a greater range of neck & head motion over other dolls of this size, which have completely cloth torsos and limited, if any, neck motion.

Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

Now I've got Scout here to take care of business. It's like a Ring doorbell on wheels.

I'm having a lot of fun controlling it manually from home. It connects to the wifi at work and I check in on things using the app. It's working very well and seems to hold a signal about 250kbps. 1080p recordings look fine. For myself, the night vision works a charm. It's clear enough to identify people, and that's all that matters. Plus, driving it around my office while I'm in bed is pretty cool, too.

Battery takes about three hours to charge out of the box and it lasts about 2hr running around the building before it goes back to the base. Most recent firmware update makes that process significantly faster, too. If you've got it on a slick surface, it might have some trouble, but it'll get plugged in eventually. Says battery runs out after an hour using only night vision, but you can set that to automatic in the app.

Around the house, the little noises are kinda neat, but for use as security, that'd be something to disable....except the alarm. That's something to keep on in case you need to scare someone off. Recording all that stuff and saving files to the phone is a plus.

I really like this little guy. It's definitely something you'll have to play around with, but it is a load of fun getting set up.

text_fidelity_a:
My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV I like this game console, but really just think it's something that a few people will enjoy more than most. The design of the console is really good, the look of the main unit is very well done. The wireless controllers are decent enough and feel well made. It's the games though that count. The games are a bit underwhelming. There is a good variety of games, from card games (solitaire, go fish, and a few others of that kind) to puzzle games (sudoku, sliding block puzzle, a pattern block puzzle). There are also many arcade style games. This model of the console does not have any of the old Data East arcade games on it. There is another version that does. The front of the box for that one will have graphics showing the Data East games.

I was sort of expecting the games on this to be the same as what is on most of these sort of consoles (famiclone games), but instead these are a bit more generic than even those. Some of the games are difficult to figure out, it took me about 10-15 minutes or experimenting to figure out how the controllers worked with the sudoku game, and even after I did - the controls were so awkward it made playing the game nearly impossible (and given that this game is timed, I never could achieve a decent time in solving the puzzle). Still, there are many that are worth playing. I think one of the reasons I like game systems like this is the challenge of figuring out what makes the game work.

The main game unit take four double A batteries and the wireless units take triple-A batteries (three each). The console hooks to the TV via a composite video cable (yellow RCA plug) and has one audio input (another RCA plug). I'm using the front inputs on my old VCR which is still connected to my television. I like that the controllers are wireless. You don't really need both, many of the games are for single player. The controllers are marked (P1 & P2), as the P1 controller is the main one and it is used to select the games from the menu.

All-in-all, I am enjoying most of these games, and appreciate the game system for what it is - but I would imagine that many people might not.

This system is made by My Arcade Gaming, and I have one of their handheld Go Gamer Portable games which I purchased last year around Christmas time. I was sort of hoping that this new game console would have the same set of games on it that their handheld model has (which are really good by the way), but that wasn't the case.
text_fidelity_b: My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV

Adora Amazing Girls 18 Doll (Amazon Exclusive), Jacqueline One of the things that I love about the Adora dolls is that each doll has her own face sculpt. The dolls look unique and not like clones with different skin tones and face paint.

The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. This allows for a greater range of neck & head motion over other dolls of this size, which have completely cloth torsos and limited, if any, neck motion.

Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

Her mouth is a unique shape and expression, not common with dolls in this space. Her shoes are cute, and her hair is very shiny.
text_fidelity_b: Adora Amazing Girls 18 Doll (Amazon Exclusive), Jacqueline

text_fidelity_a:
Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit) The Klutz kits are hit and miss for us, but this one was a hit. Now, that said, like a lot of the Klutz kits, this is a difficult one for children, and will require a very hands on adult helper.

The designs are very nice, and the instructions are good throughout if you have Google or sewing knowledge. It's not that it's going to be terribly difficult to figure out how to sew necessarily, but some of the designs are reasonably complex. I'm not a sewer, but I could figure it out, and instruct my little ones. There are a lot of steps to some of them, and the dexterity needed means that this is going to be one for the older children almost exclusively - they'll need some "advanced" skills like maintaining an even stitch pattern that is not too widely spaced or narrow, figuring out what "whip-stitching" is without it being explained thoroughly, and so forth. Because the designs are all fairly small, you can make one, then save the rest for later, and the kit will see use for many crafting sessions.

I'm very impressed by the finished product as well. Overall, a fun and educational experience for the little ones and for myself as well.
text_fidelity_b: Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit)

ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn I've bought some of the Alex Toys for the children in our family, but this is the first Alex Junior Toy we've owned. Alex Toys are known for their sturdiness, well made enough to pass on to future generations, wonderful educational and imagination values and gorgeous vivid colors. This beautiful barn is no exception with it's sturdiness, educational value and vivid bright colors.

This barn is very sturdy, weighing over 10 pounds and made of both very smooth wood and wood products. You can easily see this lasting for future generations of babies to learn with. There are 6 sides of the barn for learning and play. The 2 sides of the roof are beautifully colored with numbers and corresponding food items- such as the number 8, shows eight ears of corn. One side of the barn has 3 barn doors that when opened, baby can see the animals living inside. The other side of the barn, has a windmill, cloud and sun that, being gears, all turn each other when moved.

The large back of the barn has a moveable tractor, cow and rooster. Baby can move these inside the tracks, so nothing comes loose. The front of the barn includes the most wonderful spinning wood blocks of the alphabet with accompanying pictures. There is a darling owl for the letter O, a cute donkey for the letter D and all the pictures that accompany the letters of the alphabet are not only adorable, but beautifully colored. We have twins in our family and this barn being 6 sided allows them to play on different sides at the same time.

I remember wood alphabet blocks being passed down from one generation to another in our family, but this gorgeous barn will replace that tradition. This barn makes it easy and fun for baby to learn both the alphabet and their numbers at the same time. Our babies love the vivid colors and they love learning that 2 means counting 2 items and that the sound of the letter J sounds like Jam. This is a beautiful barn that your baby will love learning their ABC's and 123's with. It's 5 Star Learning Fun that will last many generations to come.

text_fidelity_a: Mountains Out of Molehills | Family Board Game for 2-4 Players | Two-Level Gameboard Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Great Gateway Game for Ages 9+ I was in love with this game as soon as I saw that one of the characters was a naked mole rat.  This is a 3D game with levels and "mole hills" to stack.  The setup is easy and sturdy.  You use the bottom of the box as part of the set-up.  All the pieces are well made and strong- not going to be easy to break or fold.  The art and details are amazing.  The instructions are only about 3 pages long- which is short for some of today's games.  They are easy to understand and have illustrations to keep everyone on the same page.  Another wonderful thing is that there are TWO playing modes.  One mode when you only have two people, and another for larger groups.  Games that do this are great- it means you can have as much fun and challenges playing as two people as you can with four.  It suggests ages 9+ because some of the strategy involved, though younger children could play with some guidance.  The objective for this game is to build the mole hills and control the most mountains.  Very fun to play.

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Loving Family Dollhouse As a new dad with no sisters growing up, I'm fairly new to the whole dollhouse experience. While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Seriously though, she really does love this dollhouse. I think it's pretty good for the price, as it's absolutely huge (close to 3 ft tall), but to be honest, I expected a lot more in terms of the "stuff" inside. There is some detail built into the walls, but hardly any furniture pieces that you can move around. There are some family members included, but only parents and baby, who appears to have just come from the hospital. It's a bit like a family just moving into their first apartment, where all they have is a moldy old sofa and some flowers on the wall.

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.

text_fidelity_a: SUSSED The Weird Would You Rather Card Game | Ages: Teens, Adults, Kids 12+ | 110 Cards | for Family, Friends and More | Fantasy Version Played a quick round with my wife and 6-year-old daughter as soon as it arrived.  The game is quick and easy - a scorepad, a deck of cards, and a basic set of rules.  You ask questions, on mostly random subjects, and each of the two guessers attempts to figure out what the third player is going to choose from a set of 3 options.  The vocabulary and topic selection is a little tough for a bright 6-year-old, but a little rewording from Mom and Dad helped her get through it.  Overall, it's a cute idea, but it might get old quickly with only one deck, and it has minimal replay value, as the conversation quickly turns to "I would have chosen..." which is going to deflate your desire to play through multiple times.  There's not as many questions as you'd like to see since each card has 4 questions and that constitutes a round.  I could see a game like this making a nice icebreaker for a corporate team-building retreat or a get-to-know-your-classmates style game, but for a family game, it was good, not great, and not something that we'll likely keep coming back to.
text_fidelity_b: SUSSED The Weird Would You Rather Card Game | Ages: Teens, Adults, Kids 12+ | 110 Cards | for Family, Friends and More | Fantasy Version

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack The Barbie Dream Closet is indeed a very happy dream realized. There’s so much space to store all of the clothes and accessories, as well any additional clothing items you already own for Barbie. The mini hangers work great with the clothing rack, as there’s a bit of a grip to the hooks so the hangers stay in place, but are easy to put on and take off. The system is also super convenient to carry around due to its folded design, which latches in the front with a Barbie labeled lever, and the handle on top lets this go anywhere with ease. I do love that this set encourages all sorts of ways to be fun, adventurous, sporty, fancy, and smart with the closet decals, clothes and accessories (lab coat and shoes, laptop, fancy dress with jewelry and shoes, scuba gear, etc).

A few criticisms though…the nob on top to turn the clothing rack is a bit hard to spin, both in resistance and due to the short nob. I do wish it was a little bit looser and the nob was a little bit taller to make it easier to grab.
There are a few areas that fold in and out for storage, as well as shelves to place things, but I think it would have been nice for some sort of drawer system. The drawers would have been helpful for storing the mini bracelet, necklace, hair brush, sunglasses, etc to give them a good home when not in use. Using my imagination, it would have been extra fun if the full-length mirror had a battery operated set of mini Hollywood lights to add some flare. I think some extra touches like the drawers and mirror lights would make the price worth it. I think it’s just a tad on the expensive side for it lacking some details, although it's worth reiterating that the included pieces offer a lot of good play and imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dream Closet Playset with 30+ Clothes and Accessories Including 5 Outfits, Plus Mirror, Desk and Rotating Rack
